_comment_family: The Regular, and fitness-story-de's block face. Its picked words are
set in acumin-pro-bold — the same family's 700 — so the two are told
apart by weight alone.
Acumin is Adobe's neo-grotesque: an Akzidenz descendant drawn on the
same bones as Helvetica, with a large x-height and flat, closed
terminals. That lineage is the whole of why the fallbacks below are
what they are, and it is the reason a missing file here does less
visible damage than it does to the display faces in this folder —
which is not the same as doing none.
Declared as the bare family name, and this is the one pack in the
folder where that is the honest answer rather than a shortcut. The
two Acumin files share name ID 1 ('Acumin Pro') the way the two
Telegraf files share theirs, so by the rule telegraf-ultralight sets
out each should be declared under its full name instead — except
that this file's full name (ID 4) IS 'Acumin Pro'. A RIBBI family's
Regular has no name of its own to be declared under; the family name
is its full name, and inventing one would be declaring a face under
a name nothing on any machine answers to.
What keeps that from colliding with the Bold is the weight. This
face is registered at 400 and the Bold declares a different CSS
family entirely ('Acumin Pro Bold', its own ID 4), so the canvas
asking for `400 40px "Acumin Pro"` can only reach this file and
nothing asks for 'Acumin Pro' at 700 at all. The one place the
sharing still costs something is `local` below, which is where it is
dealt with.
Weight 400, which is what the file's OS/2 table says.
_comment_css: Not declared in styles.css: this face arrived with a channel and is
registered from this JSON, which is the route content/README.md
describes. Nothing has to be added to the stylesheet for it.
_comment_local: What the machine may already know the face by, tried after the file.
One name and not the usual two. The PostScript name is here, and it
is also what the installer registers the face under (see
engine.install_fonts, which takes the first entry). The Windows full
name is deliberately absent, because for this cut it is the string
'Acumin Pro' — the family name the Bold carries as well. A machine
with the full Acumin family installed could answer that name with
any weight of it, and a fallback that may hand back the Bold is not
a fallback for the Regular. The PostScript name has no such
ambiguity: it names this cut and only this cut.
The cost of dropping it is nothing on a machine this app installed
on — the installed copy is registered as 'AcuminPro-Regular', which
is the name that is still listed.
_comment_stack: The fallbacks are damage limitation and never a design choice — a
caption laid out against the wrong metrics is broken, not merely
different, which is what fontguard exists to catch before it is ever
drawn. They are still chosen rather than copied: Acumin is an
Akzidenz-line grotesque, so Arial — a Helvetica clone from the same
line, present on every Windows this app runs on — is both the
nearest shape and the nearest set width, and Segoe UI stands behind
it. Impact and Arial Black are absent for telegraf-ultralight's
reason: they are heavy display cuts, and putting one behind a
400-weight text grotesque would make the one thing that survives a
missing file the furthest possible thing from it.
